question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, we compute the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\frac{5}{8}\times 3-(8-10)^{-3}=\frac{5}{8}\times 3-(-2)^{-3}
$$

Next, notice that $(-2)^{-3}=\frac{1}{(-2)^{3}}=-\frac{1}{8}.$ So, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{8}\times 3-(-2)^{-3} & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\times 3-(-\frac{1}{8}) & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\times \frac{3}{1}+\frac{1}{8} & = \\ \frac{5\times 3}{8\times 1}+\frac{1}{8} & = \\ \frac{15}{8}+\frac{1}{8} & = \\ \frac{15+1}{8} & = \\ \frac{16}{8} & = \\ 2\end{aligned}
$$
